def event_params
  # Permit title, description, and array of user IDs
  permitted = params.require(:event).permit(:title, :description, assigned_user_ids: [])
  
  # Process assigned_user_ids array
  if permitted[:assigned_user_ids].present?
    # Remove empty strings and convert to integers

  end
  
  return permitted
end

implementation.name: JsonplaceholderService#fetch_users
implementation.pseudo_code:
def self.fetch_users
  # Check cache first (5-minute duration)
  Rails.cache.fetch('jsonplaceholder_users', expires_in: CACHE_DURATION) do
    uri = URI("#{BASE_URL}/users")
    response = Net::HTTP.get_response(uri)
    
    if response.code == '200'
      # Parse and return user array
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      # Return empty array on failure
      return []
    end
  rescue => e
    # Log error and return empty array
    Rails.logger.error("Error fetching users: #{e.message}")
    return []
  end
end

def assigned_user_ids
  value = read_attribute(:assigned_user_ids)
  return [] if value.blank?
  JSON.parse(value) rescue []
end

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Creates the events table with columns: id, title (string, not null), description (text), created_at, updated_at. Stores the core event data and created_at timestamp used for ordering events newest-first in AC2.
implementation.name: CreateEvents migration
implementation.pseudo_code:
create_table :events do |t|
  t.string :title, null: false
  t.text :description
  t.timestamps
end

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Sets root path to events#index, making the events listing the home page. Also defines resources :events which generates RESTful routes for all event actions. This enables AC9 (event list accessible from Home page) and provides routes for View/Edit/Remove actions.
implementation.name: Routes configuration
implementation.pseudo_code:
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  root "events#index"
  resources :events
end
